actualPrimaryReadings.sourceFinding: Actual Haushaltstheorie names utility theory, homo oeconomicus and restricted rational behaviour through preferences. The accompanying competence paragraph includes model construction and reasoned conclusions from targeted model changes. The authored Source125 household row is a derived aspect, not a verbatim official quote. Attention menus are a bounded authored mechanism implementation, not proof that the official text names a particular default effect or experiment.

E2.6 includes analysis of decision situations, own interest versus ecological/social responsibility, factors such as budget and information asymmetry. The AB1 seed is a sourceSnapshotGoal, not the official classification of every P task or a claim that all state curricula impose this atom.

requiredClauseAudit.text: Haushaltsnachfrage kann im vereinfachten Nutzen-/Homo-Modell als höchstgereihtes bezahlbares Bündel bei ausdrücklich gegebenen konsistenten Präferenzen erklärt werden. Die Ordnung ist nur ordinal und individuell, keine objektive oder zwischen Personen addierbare Nutzenmenge. Vollständige Kenntnis und Beachtung aller Möglichkeiten sind idealisierte Annahmen; knappes Budget, eingeschränkte Information und Aufmerksamkeit sowie andere legitime Präferenzen sind auseinanderzuhalten.
requiredClauseAudit.finding: Supported bounded conceptual demand explanation. The complete rankings are given and only ordinal; selecting the highest-ranked affordable offered bundle explains needs/preferences and a budget restriction. No learner must derive a utility function, prove optimisation, measure universal utility, or recall an unprovided model.

requiredClauseAudit.text: Die Person erläutert an zwei konkreten Haushaltsnachfragen die bezahlbaren Bündel, ausdrückliche Präferenzannahmen und idealisierte Auswahl; sie diskutiert eine echte Preis-/Budgetvariation und einen kontrollierten Informations-/Aufmerksamkeitsmechanismus, ohne unterschiedliche Bedürfnisse pauschal als Verzerrung auszugeben.
requiredClauseAudit.finding: The required performance discusses given feasible choices, stated preference assumptions, a price/budget change and a bounded information/attention mechanism. These remain explanations of consumer patterns through needs, budget and information. The clause does not require a general bias taxonomy, psychological diagnosis, empirical study, elasticity or a separate successor goal.

Both expectation IDs are mandatory and must actually be evidenced. The integer two is a minimum independent-demonstration count for the whole profile; it is not an instruction to complete all four case briefs. The second expectation names two concrete household choices, which can share evidence with the first expectation. Two arbitrary responses are not guaranteed sufficient if responsibility or another required facet is still missing. The required evidence, rather than the case IDs or an extra-task quota, determines sufficiency.

requiredClauseAudit.text: Verwende einen fiktiven Einpersonenhaushalt statt privater Daten. Für die flexible Wochenentscheidung nach gesondert gedeckten Grundausgaben stehen 10 Euro bereit. Der örtliche Anbieter verkauft ausschließlich fünf feste Wochenpakete aus Obstportionen x (2 Euro je Portion) und Freizeittickets y (4 Euro je Ticket): A=(3,1), B=(1,2), C=(1,1), D=(0,2), E=(2,0). Die im Modell offengelegte gesamte Präferenzordnung von Lea lautet A>B>D>C>E; sie umfasst auch die Bewertung des jeweils übrigbleibenden Geldes. Erkläre ihre Nachfrage zunächst mit Nutzentheorie und dem hier ausdrücklich idealisierten homo oeconomicus: feste widerspruchsfreie Präferenzen, bekannte Preise, vollständige Kenntnis aller fünf angebotenen Pakete und Wahl des höchstgereihten bezahlbaren Pakets. Es gibt keine messbare allgemeingültige Nutzenzahl. Prüfe danach bei unveränderten Präferenzen eine Preissteigerung der Obstportion auf 3 Euro und diskutiere die Nachfrageänderung. In einer weiteren Situation bei den ursprünglichen Preisen sieht Lea unter Zeitdruck nur die erste Bildschirmseite mit B,C,D,E; A steht unverändert zum selben Preis auf der zweiten Seite und wird nicht geprüft. Unter den beachteten Paketen wählt sie das bevorzugte B. Ein gleichbleibender Vergleich zeigt alle fünf Pakete gleichzeitig bei denselben Bedürfnissen, Präferenzen und Preisen. Erläutere die Grenze des Idealmodells und was der Vergleich über eingeschränkte Information/Aufmerksamkeit prüfen könnte. Mila hat bei vollständiger Information die legitime Ordnung B>A>C>E>D und wählt B. Erkläre, weshalb ihre abweichende Präferenz allein kein Bias-Beweis ist.
requiredClauseAudit.finding: This case supplies the menu, full preference order including leftover money, full-information reference assumptions, prices, budget, considered set and a matched-menu counterfactual. Explaining A then D, or B within the considered subset, uses those supplied inputs. Explaining the provided comparison is a conceptual model contrast, not independently constructing or executing an experiment.

requiredClauseAudit.text: Another fictional household can spend EUR 12 from its leisure budget; all other spending is funded outside this explicitly restricted model. The only available monthly plans contain film rentals f(EUR 3) and swimming visits s(EUR 6): A=(2,1), B=(0,2), C=(3,0), D=(1,1), E=(1,0). The person’s complete preference order is A>D>B>C>E and includes leftover money. Use an ordinal utility representation to explain why known prices, full information and consistent selection make A the ideal model’s predicted demand bundle. Examine the highest-ranked affordable bundle when the film price rises to EUR 4 with the same budget/preferences. At original prices, a preselected button instead shows B; during 15 seconds the person considers only B and C and chooses B because B is preferred to C. All other plans could be reached in the same list without extra costs. Reflect on omitted information/attention in this fictional personal choice relative to the reference model and devise a matched comparison. Another fully informed person ranks B>A>D>C>E because swimming matters more to them. Is that person’s B-choice also a demonstrated bias? Explain without inventing objective total utility or a single correct preference.
requiredClauseAudit.finding: The phrase devise a matched comparison is more constructive than the German reflect on a suitable neutral comparison, but its bounded expected performance provides the actual comparison: same prices/goals, all A–E visible and adequate attention. As an application brief it does not add a separate required-expectation ID or an independent experimental-method mastery contract. Optional future bilingual tidying could say discuss a suitable matched comparison; that is not a necessary scope remedy.

wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.core: Feasibility depends on the current budget and the commute need; different purchases do not prove irrationality.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.adversarialWrong: The pass is fashionable, therefore both should buy it.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.ownAdequate: A longer commute can make the pass valuable, but its upfront cost can make it infeasible. Repairing a bicycle may fit another commute and budget. The same leisure purchase does not by itself reveal either learner’s motives.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.scopeFinding: Within ordinary needs/budget explanation; opportunity-cost reasoning names the forgone alternative and does not require a separate formal theory or measurement prerequisite.

wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.core: Upfront affordability, lifetime information and legitimate environmental weighting can point in different directions.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.adversarialWrong: The durable option is always rational because its annual cost must be lower.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.ownAdequate: The durable option may reduce lifetime expenditure yet exceed the buyer’s available money now; without durability data its savings are uncertain. Environmental priorities can legitimately change a preference ranking. The choice does not establish deficient rationality.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.scopeFinding: HE E2.6 provides actual source support for own interest, social/ecological responsibility, budget and information. No automatic requirement to master the sustainable-consumption successor follows from discussing these supplied features.

wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.core: Given menu/ranking: A at original prices; D after the specified price change. B from a limited considered set differs from another person’s fully informed B preference.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.adversarialWrong: Choosing B proves bias and the price rise universally eliminates fruit demand.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.ownAdequate: A is originally affordable and first in Lea’s given order. After the specified fruit-price rise, A and B exceed the budget; D ranks above the remaining feasible C and E. With only B,C,D,E considered, B is consistent with Lea’s ranking. Showing all five unchanged packages together could examine the specified exclusion of A. Mila’s complete B-first order instead supports a legitimate taste difference. This finite menu does not establish a general demand law.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.scopeFinding: The steps execute a supplied introductory model rather than autonomous optimisation, outside mathematical prerequisites, measured interpersonal utility or a real bias diagnosis.

wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.core: A at original prices, D when films cost EUR 4; B in subset B,C is not evidence that a fully informed B-preferring person is biased.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.adversarialWrong: A is the objectively highest-utility choice for everyone and the default proves irrationality.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.ownAdequate: A is the first feasible plan under the given original ranking. At the higher film price it exceeds the budget, so D is highest among the remaining plans. B beats C within the stated considered set. A comparison with all A–E visible, the same needs/prices and sufficient viewing time examines the specified model assumption; a B choice alone identifies no cause. A different complete B-first ranking makes B legitimate.
wholeFourCaseAdversarialChecks.scopeFinding: A simple supplied counterfactual about access to alternatives remains a consumer-decision explanation. It does not impose mastery of bounded rationality across unprovided settings or a general experimental-design method.

successorBoundary: The native graph identifies practiceAssessment Nachfrage, Präferenzen und begrenzte Aufmerksamkeit and a curricular Begrenzte Rationalität in Entscheidungen erklären successor. Their titles alone do not establish exclusive ownership of every attention-related explanation. No audited mandatory P clause requires independently mastering either entire successor. Source-bound introductory consumer explanation may share concepts with later practice and broader conceptual goals without requiring their full mastery.
taxonomyAssessment: The existing ordinary E/AB1 contract remains introductory, supplied-model explanation: menu, ranks, assumptions and choice rule are explicitly provided. Finite affordability and ranking checks and discussion of a supplied counterfactual do not introduce an unprovided general optimisation or scientific-method competence. This audit supports retaining the current taxonomy; it does not assert that AB1 is an official Berlin label for the entire cited source paragraph or that future unscaffolded investigations would remain in scope.
